title: [Bug] PrefillDelayer can enter a persistent mixed-state feedback loop and collapse prefill progress under DP Attention + chunked prefill
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues / PRs and did not find one matching this exact failure mode.
- [x] The issue is reproducible across repeated runs with the same server/client configuration.
- [x] Requests complete successfully; this is primarily a scheduler / performance-stability issue rather than a model-correctness failure.
- [x] I compared the behavior against `PrefillDelayer` disabled and inspected the relevant scheduler / delayer source code.
- [x] I collected per-DP-rank scheduler metrics and prefill-progress counters.

---

## Summary

Under a long-prefill workload with:

- DeepSeek-V4-Pro
- TP=8
- DP=8
- DP Attention enabled
- chunked prefill enabled
- PrefillDelayer enabled
- one 8-GPU node

an identical server configuration and deterministic workload can enter two qualitatively different runtime regimes:

### Healthy synchronized state

- Input throughput: ~94.6–94.8k tok/s
- DP ranks progress through prefill nearly in lockstep
- `PrefillDelayer` converges to sustained `all / no_wait`
- average running requests is ~8.5

### Pathological LOW state

- Input throughput: ~62–79k tok/s
- within the first ~5 s of the formal workload, DP-rank prefill progress diverges by an integer number of effective prefill chunks
- the first observed spread is typically exactly **16384 tokens**, i.e. one effective per-rank chunk
- `PrefillDelayer` remains dominated by `mixed / delay`
- average running requests collapses to ~0.15
- residual / under-filled prefill batches increase sharply

This is not explained by persistent per-rank request-count imbalance. In one representative LOW run, the first 30 s admitted exactly the same number of sequences on all 8 DP ranks, yet rank-level prefill progress had already diverged by one full chunk within 5 s.

Disabling `PrefillDelayer` does **not** recover the healthy state. Instead, the system enters a third regime with lower but more continuous concurrency:

- throughput: ~48–68k tok/s
- avg running requests: ~4.7–5.9
- residual batches: ~11–14%

Therefore the LOW state with PrefillDelayer enabled is not equivalent to "PrefillDelayer disabled". It appears to be a distinct scheduler regime in which the delayer participates in suppressing prefill progress.

The exact upstream trigger is still being localized. I am opening this issue because the observed `mixed/delay` feedback loop appears different from the already-known `all/slot_condition` starvation fixed in #29898.

---

## Environment

```text
SGLang version : 0.5.14
commit         : 49e384ce9d304648e9959666ecb8ce8cd98d0deb
git log -1     : 49e384c [Cherry-pick to release/v0.5.14] Revert Gemma4 modelopt fp4 MoE backend change (#28347) (#29246)
git describe   : v0.5.14
remote         : https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang.git
local patches  : no tracked-file modifications
```

The earlier scheduler-debug instrumentation was fully reverted before the measurements described here. The remaining untracked files were only local backup files / an empty accidental file; tracked scheduler source matched the clean release tree.

Hardware / topology:

```text
1 node
8 × NVIDIA B30Z
TP = 8
DP = 8
DP Attention = enabled
MoE A2A backend = MegaMoE
```

Relevant server configuration:

```bash
--tp 8
--dp 8
--enable-dp-attention
--enable-prefill-delayer
--chunked-prefill-size 131072
```

With DP Attention, the effective per-rank prefill chunk is:

```text
131072 / 8 = 16384 tokens
```

Relevant MegaMoE cap:

```bash
SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=16512
```

Workload:

```text
input length    : 60000
output length   : 1
max concurrency : 16
num prompts     : 160
ignore_eos      : true
seed            : 1
```

The 60k prompt is therefore processed approximately as:

```text
16384 + 16384 + 16384 + remainder
```

The client workload is burst-style; no request-rate throttling or intentional staggering is used in the baseline.

---

## Reproduction behavior

Representative post-reboot runs:

| Run | Input TPS | Median TTFT | avg running | avg queue | residual batches |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| good | 94,634 | 9.66 s | 8.13 | 0.16 | 11.96% |
| LOW | 72,923 | 12.38 s | 0.17 | 0.84 | 27.17% |
| LOW | 62,379 | 13.81 s | 0.12 | 0.85 | 29.03% |
| good | 94,690 | 9.65 s | 8.37 | 0.17 | 9.52% |
| mid | 82,688 | 9.68 s | 5.90 | 0.29 | 12.81% |
| LOW | 78,571 | 10.45 s | 0.24 | 0.84 | 28.41% |

The healthy-state throughput is extremely stable (~94.6k tok/s, sub-percent variation), while LOW runs have a qualitatively different scheduler signature rather than ordinary run-to-run noise.

A host reboot did not eliminate the problem.

---

## Observation 1: LOW starts as a rank-level prefill-progress divergence

Using the per-rank counter:

```text
sglang:realtime_tokens_total{dp_rank="...", mode="prefill_compute"}
```

I computed:

```text
progress_spread(t) = max_i(prefill_tokens_i(t)) - min_i(prefill_tokens_i(t))
```

Results:

| Run | TPS | spread@5s | spread@10s | spread@15s | spread@20s | spread@30s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| good | 94,634 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| good | 94,690 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| mid | 82,688 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| LOW | 72,923 | 16k | 22k | 27k | 11k | 16k |
| LOW | 62,379 | 16k | 16k | 60k | 60k | 60k |
| LOW | 78,571 | 16k | 22k | 27k | 0 | 0 |

The important feature is that the first LOW-state divergence is quantized at approximately:

```text
16384 tokens
```

which is exactly one effective prefill chunk.

`realtime_tokens_total` is incremented from `report_prefill_stats()` after a prefill batch result is processed, so this metric represents completed/reported prefill progress. It does **not** by itself prove whether the original cause was scheduler suppression or slower GPU execution.

### Metric-cadence validation

I separately validated the observable cadence of `realtime_tokens_total` using 0.2 s scrapes during a smaller N32/C16 run with the same 16k effective chunk.

Across all ranks:

```text
jump interval p50 = 1.397 s
jump interval p95 = 1.535 s
min interval       = 0.401 s
```

Jump-size distribution:

```text
16384 ×112   (one full chunk)
11264 ×8     (tail chunks)
256   ×3     (small startup fragments)
32768 ×0     (no two-chunk merge observed)
```

Thus the progress-spread observation is not an artifact of multiple 16k completions being collapsed into one scrape sample in this validation run.

---

## Observation 2: persistent request-count imbalance is not required for LOW

I counted per-rank `#new-seq` admissions during the first 30 s of the formal workload.

| Run | r0 | r1 | r2 | r3 | r4 | r5 | r6 | r7 | range | CV |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| good | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 27 | 26 | 26 | 1 | 1.4% |
| good | 26 | 25 | 25 | 25 | 25 | 25 | 25 | 26 | 1 | 1.8% |
| mid | 27 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 1 | 1.4% |
| LOW | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | **0** | **0.0%** |
| LOW | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 17 | 17 | 18 | 18 | 1 | 2.6% |
| LOW | 14 | 15 | 10 | 14 | 10 | 14 | 13 | 14 | 5 | 14.8% |

The strongest case is the 72.9k TPS LOW run:

```text
18 18 18 18 18 18 18 18
```

All eight ranks admitted exactly the same number of sequences during the first 30 s, yet prefill progress had already diverged by one 16k chunk at 5 s.

Therefore persistent per-rank request-count imbalance is not a necessary condition for entering the LOW state.

Sub-second request-arrival / dispatch timing skew is **not** ruled out by this measurement. Also, `#new-seq` is scheduler admission into a prefill batch, not a direct counter of the initial DataParallelController request dispatch.

---

## Observation 3: PrefillDelayer state strongly separates healthy and LOW runs

From:

```text
sglang:prefill_delayer_outcomes_total
```

healthy runs eventually converge to sustained:

```text
input_estimation="all"
output_reason="no_wait"
```

while LOW runs remain dominated by:

```text
input_estimation="mixed"
output_reason="delay"
```

In healthy runs, after an initial transient, `mixed/delay` can disappear for long intervals and all 8 ranks repeatedly observe an immediately releasable state.

In LOW runs, `mixed/delay` remains persistent and the scheduler never establishes the same synchronized regime.

I use:

```text
all_no_wait / (all_no_wait + mixed_delay)
```

only as a diagnostic state index, not as a literal request-release probability, because `mixed/delay` may be counted repeatedly across multiple scheduler passes during one waiting episode.

The observed behavior is best described as synchronization / phase-locking-like behavior; I am not claiming a formal oscillator model.

---

## Observation 4: LOW is not equivalent to disabling PrefillDelayer

I ran a separate six-run experiment with the same 16k effective chunk but with PrefillDelayer disabled.

| Run | Input TPS | avg running | residual batches | median TTFT |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 67,658 | 5.65 | 11.78% | 12.62 s |
| 2 | 48,536 | 4.73 | 12.01% | 15.11 s |
| 3 | 53,299 | 5.26 | 11.18% | 15.43 s |
| 4 | 64,174 | 5.36 | 12.24% | 13.29 s |
| 5 | 55,500 | 4.69 | 14.04% | 15.70 s |
| 6 | 64,715 | 5.90 | 12.02% | 13.10 s |

Mean throughput:

```text
58,980 tok/s
CV = 12.88%
```

The important mechanism difference is:

```text
PrefillDelayer ON, healthy : avg running ≈ 8.5
PrefillDelayer ON, deep LOW: avg running ≈ 0.15
PrefillDelayer OFF         : avg running ≈ 4.7–5.9
```

Thus the ON-LOW state is not simply the delayer becoming ineffective and behaving like OFF. The delayer-enabled LOW regime suppresses running concurrency far more aggressively than the OFF regime.

This OFF experiment was not interleaved with the ON runs, so I do **not** use it to estimate relative state-entry probabilities. I also do not claim six samples prove a statistically unimodal OFF distribution. The robust observation is the mechanism-signature difference above.

---

## Observation 5: staggered arrivals make the failure worse

As a diagnostic experiment, I changed the formal client traffic from a burst to:

```text
2 requests/s, fixed interval
```

while keeping concurrency=16.

This was intentionally stopped after the direction was clearly harmful.

Representative results:

```text
burst: 94,630 tok/s
ramp : 53,449 tok/s

burst: 64,016 tok/s
ramp : LOW again
```

The ramp sends approximately one new request every 0.5 s. With DP=8 this naturally exposes only a subset of ranks to new work at a time, increasing the probability that the delayer observes a `mixed` state.

This is not presented as a production benchmark because the arrival process itself changed. It is included because the behavior is consistent with the delayer being highly sensitive to cross-rank arrival phase.

Related newer work such as #35191 independently discusses trickle arrivals and persistent fragmented prefills, although that PR operates on a newer optional queue-trigger path that is not enabled in this configuration.

---

## Local source comparison against later upstream fixes

I compared this exact `v0.5.14` tree against several later PrefillDelayer / scheduler fixes.

### 1. #29898 — missing locally

The local `PrefillDelayer` has a bounded delay in the `mixed` branch:

```python
prev_delayed_count = prev_state.delayed_count if prev_state else 0
if prev_delayed_count < self._max_delay_passes - 1:
    ...
    output_reason="delay"
else:
    ...
    output_reason="wait_timeout"
```

but its `all` branch can still delay indefinitely when `slot_condition` or `queue_condition` remains true:

```python
if slot_condition or queue_condition:
    ...
    next_state = next_state.bump_delayed_count()
    return _NegotiateOutput(
        output_allow=False,
        output_reason="delay",
        ...
    )
```

with no equivalent `max_delay_passes` bound.

This confirms that the local tree predates #29898.

However, I do **not** claim #29898 is the direct cause here: in the collected workload, `all/delay` was not observed; the pathological state is dominated by `mixed/delay`.

Its relevance is that upstream has independently confirmed that PrefillDelayer feedback can cause prefill starvation and running-batch collapse.

---

### 2. #31835 — current reproduction hits the older negotiation placement

The local `schedule_policy.py` contains two paths:

```text
add_one_req_ignore_eos()  -> negotiation after budget/admission checks
add_one_req()             -> negotiation at the beginning of the function
```

The dispatch condition is:

```python
if req.sampling_params.ignore_eos and getattr(self.tree_cache, "disable", True):
    return self.add_one_req_ignore_eos(req)
```

This reproduction has:

```text
ignore_eos = true
radix cache enabled -> tree_cache.disable = false
```

so the condition is false and the workload falls through to `add_one_req()`.

In the local tree, `add_one_req()` begins with:

```python
if (self.prefill_delayer_single_pass is not None) and (
    not self.prefill_delayer_single_pass.negotiate_should_allow_prefill(
        local_prefillable=True,
        running_batch=self.running_batch.batch_size(),
        max_prefill_bs=self.max_prefill_bs,
        max_running_requests=self.max_running_requests,
        waiting_queue_len=self.waiting_queue_len,
    )
):
    return AddReqResult.OTHER
```

before later request / chunk / admission checks.

Therefore, on the actual reproduction path, `local_prefillable=True` is sampled before all subsequent admission checks. The alternate `add_one_req_ignore_eos()` path samples after budget checks, so the two paths have different semantics.

This is directly relevant to interpretation of `all/mixed`: `local_prefillable` is a scheduler-side estimate whose meaning depends on where it is sampled, not a direct GPU-readiness signal.

That said, I do **not** currently think this semantic issue alone explains the LOW state. In the failing workload, KV/SWA pressure is very low (observed full-pool usage ~0.55%, SWA usage ~2.74%), so most post-negotiation admission checks are unlikely to fail. The placement issue is therefore real in this path but not yet demonstrated to be the active trigger.

---

### 3. #30295 — key chunked-request double-count shape is still present

The local scheduler already contains an early guard:

```python
if (
    self.get_num_allocatable_reqs(running_bs) <= 0
    and self.chunked_req is None
    ...
):
```

but the later waiting-queue loop still contains:

```python
if len(adder.can_run_list) >= self.get_num_allocatable_reqs(running_bs):
    self.running_batch.batch_is_full = True
```

while `add_chunked_req(...)` adds the in-flight chunked request to `self.can_run_list`, and `get_num_allocatable_reqs()` uses:

```python
min(
    pp_max_micro_batch_size - running_bs,
    req_to_token_pool.available_size(),
)
```

where the in-flight request's slot is already reflected in `available_size()`.

This preserves the shape of the later double-count fixed by #30295.

I do not think this alone explains the reported collapse: #30295 causes a stable one-slot loss, whereas the LOW state here collapses avg running from approximately 8.5 to approximately 0.15. It may still be an adjacent bug or amplification factor.

---

### 4. #24768 — present locally, but current configuration uses CPU/Gloo negotiation

The local tree contains the NCCL/device-group option for PrefillDelayer synchronization.

With the current settings:

```text
disable_overlap_schedule = false
SGLANG_NCCL_ALL_GATHER_IN_OVERLAP_SCHEDULER_SYNC_BATCH = false
```

PrefillDelayer uses the CPU/Gloo negotiation path.

Enabling the NCCL synchronization path in this MegaMoE configuration was not stable in my environment and led to an NVLink/barrier timeout, so it is not currently usable as a workaround.

If the failure is ultimately localized to scheduler/readiness coordination, this cross-DP negotiation path is one area I plan to investigate further.

---

### 5. #35191 — not directly active, but relevant to the dynamics

This newer work describes a separate PrefillDelayer problem where trickle arrivals can keep the observed batching target small and sustain fragmented prefills.

The optional queue-trigger feature involved there is not enabled in this workload (`queue_min_ratio` unset), so this is not a direct code-path match.

It is nevertheless consistent with the observation here that staggered arrivals strongly destabilize synchronized prefill behavior.

---

## Current interpretation

The strongest evidence currently supports this descriptive sequence:

```text
formal workload begins
        ↓
DP ranks initially receive approximately balanced request counts
        ↓
within the first few seconds,
per-rank prefill progress diverges by an integer prefill-chunk amount
        ↓
PrefillDelayer repeatedly observes mixed states
        ↓
mixed/delay persists
        ↓
under-filled / residual batches increase
        ↓
running concurrency collapses
        ↓
LOW throughput state becomes self-sustaining
```

One causal distinction is still unresolved:

### Hypothesis B — execution-duration divergence

One or more ranks receive comparable forward work but their GPU forward takes longer:

```text
same/similar forward opportunity
        ↓
one rank completes later
        ↓
prefill progress diverges
        ↓
Delayer subsequently observes mixed
```

### Hypothesis C — scheduler/readiness suppression

The scheduler / delayer gives some ranks fewer forward opportunities:

```text
scheduler readiness / negotiation diverges
        ↓
Delayer suppresses some prefill admissions
        ↓
those ranks do less forward work
        ↓
prefill progress diverges
```

I am instrumenting:

```text
sglang:realtime_tokens_total{dp_rank,mode="prefill_compute"}
```

together with:

```text
sglang:forward_execution_seconds_total{dp_rank,category}
```

using `SGLANG_ENABLE_METRICS_DEVICE_TIMER=1`.

The DeviceTimer implementation uses CUDA events plus non-blocking `end_event.query()` rather than `synchronize()`, but I am first validating that enabling the timer itself does not perturb this timing-sensitive synchronization state.

The intended discriminator is **not** event timestamp ordering, because Delayer negotiation necessarily precedes forward completion in the source code. Instead, the discriminator is the per-rank relationship between:

```text
Δprefill_progress
and
Δcompleted_forward_execution_time
```

over a short window after the first rank-level progress divergence.

Roughly:

```text
ΔP lower and ΔF proportionally lower
→ rank likely completed less forward work
→ supports scheduler/readiness-side cause

ΔP lower but ΔF similar or higher
→ rank spent comparable/more GPU time for less progress
→ supports execution-duration-side cause
```

This follow-up work is ongoing and is not required for the observations reported above.

---

## Why I think this deserves a separate issue

I could not find an upstream issue matching all of these properties together:

```text
DP Attention
+ PrefillDelayer
+ chunked long-prefill workload
+ same deterministic configuration
+ healthy ~94.8k state vs persistent LOW state
+ LOW dominated by mixed/delay
+ avg running collapsing near zero
+ rank progress diverging by exactly one effective prefill chunk
+ request-count admission remaining balanced in at least one LOW reproduction
```

#29898 is the closest known failure family, but it is specifically an `all / slot_condition` liveness bug.

The behavior reported here appears to be a different `mixed`-branch feedback failure mode.

---

## Questions for maintainers

1. Is a persistent `mixed/delay` loop with very low `num_running_reqs` an expected / known failure mode of PrefillDelayer?

2. Are there known cases where the cross-DP `local_prefillable` negotiation can remain phase-shifted even when request counts are balanced across DP ranks?

3. Is there a known interaction between chunked prefill, an in-flight `chunked_req`, `can_run_list`, `batch_is_full`, and PrefillDelayer state that can create a self-reinforcing mixed state?

4. Would you expect #29898 / #31835 / #30295 to materially change this workload even though the observed state is primarily `mixed/delay` rather than `all/delay`?

5. Is there a recommended way to trace the first divergence between per-rank PrefillDelayer negotiation, prefill admission, and model-forward execution without materially perturbing scheduler timing?

---

## Additional data available

I retained:

- per-run server logs
- per-rank Prefill batch logs
- `#new-seq` / `#new-token` traces
- 0.2 s Prometheus cadence captures
- per-rank `realtime_tokens_total`
- PrefillDelayer outcome counters
- queue/running-request counters
- host/GPU telemetry
- good-state and LOW-state profiling artifacts

I can provide a reduced reproduction package or additional per-rank timelines if useful.
